descriptions.value:
The 'Their Finest Hour' archive contains approx. 2000 records and more than 25,000 files - including some stories/objects relating to:
Prisoners of War in Germany (https://portal.sds.ox.ac.uk/search?q=:keyword:%20%22POW%22)
Kindertransport (https://portal.sds.ox.ac.uk/search?q=Kindertransport&groups=52902)
Experiences of refugees in the UK (https://portal.sds.ox.ac.uk/search?q=%3Akeyword%3A%20%22Refugee%22&groups=52902)
Accounts of soldiers who were present at or immediately following the libreration of concentration camps (https://portal.sds.ox.ac.uk/search?q=%3Akeyword%3A%20%22Concentration%20Camp%22&groups=52902)
Second World War internment in the UK (https://portal.sds.ox.ac.uk/articles/online_resource/Betty_and_Franz_Hausner_s_Stories_as_Enemy_Aliens_/25923196)

Relevant collections include:
Records of John Norman Davey, 1916 – 2006, Including photographs of Verden military camp and Stalag X-B, Sandbostal (POW camp)
https://archives.bristol.gov.uk/records/45152
Correspondence with the Lord Mayor relating to refugees, 1930s-40s
https://archives.bristol.gov.uk/records/LM/C/X16/2
Hortham Colony album of photographs, programmes, newscuttings etc., including wartime circulars and literature, messages from British prisoners of war in Germany, 1932 – 1950
https://archives.bristol.gov.uk/records/40686/H/Ph/1/a
Letter to 'Dear family Dicks' from Harald Gorling, a German prisoner of war to whom they had given hospitality, on his return to Hannover. 1947 Sep 26
https://archives.bristol.gov.uk/records/42601/1/13
Oral testimonies including:
https://becc.bristol.gov.uk/records/OH/0777---OH-0779
https://becc.bristol.gov.uk/records/OH/0692
https://becc.bristol.gov.uk/records/OH/0231---OH-0232
https://becc.bristol.gov.uk/records/OH/CS-13---CS-14
Brunel University holds the archives of Professor Heinz Wolff https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/a/A13532145

The Department of Archives and Modern Manuscripts at Cambridge University Library holds two collections relating to refugees from Germany and Austria from the 1930s onwards. Online catalogues are available at:
https://archivesearch.lib.cam.ac.uk/repositories/2/resources/7408
and
https://archivesearch.lib.cam.ac.uk/repositories/2/resources/7742

Relevant items are located throughout the collections that can be searched at https://archivesearch.lib.cam.ac.uk/
There is also the archive of the Jewish lawyer Hersch Lauterpacht who was involved in the Nuremberg trials and the Kindertransport (https://archivesearch.lib.cam.ac.uk/repositories/9/resources/1640), Lord Kilmuir, one of the prosecutors at Nuremberg, Sir James Headlam, George Pitt-Rivers, and the Churchill papers.

Collections include:
Levison Papers https://reed.dur.ac.uk/xtf/view?docId=ark/32150_s1t435gd04h.xml
Georg Backhaus https://reed.dur.ac.uk/xtf/view?docId=ark/32150_s1c821gj771.xml#ehdlmmly-1093

Collections include:
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D7501 Records of the Gloucester Association for Aiding Refugees, 1938-1945: relating to the establishment of a hostel at 18 Alexandra Road, Gloucester, for the reception and care of refugees from the Nazi regime in central Europe, including 10 German Jewish boys aged between 12 and 14 who had arrived in the UK via the Kindertransport, and material relating to outreach projects and other legacy events.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D15077 Oral history interviews with Arnold Ullmann and Michael Zorek, son of Werner Zorek, 2019 (Arnold Ullmann and Werner Zorek were two of the Kindertransport boys accommodated by GAAR).
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D16060 Research material into the Kindertransport hostel at 18 Alexandra Road, Gloucester, and award of blue plaque status to the building, 2022.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D12376 Personal records of Ilse Majer-Williams, who arrived in the UK via the Kindertransport and eventually settled in Gloucestershire.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GBR/9/6/23/823 File of the Mayor of Gloucester concerning assistance given to Jewish refugees from Nazi Germany.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D3883 Records of Cheltenham Hebrew Congregation, 1809-2013 (mostly not relating to the Holocaust but including some uncatalogued material and some papers about commemoration of Holocaust Memorial Day; included here for completeness).
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D14926 Oral history interview with Anthony Pitt, 2019, who worked processing compensation claims from victims of the Holocaust.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D12368/1/5 Video interview with Bert Layton [born Herbert Levy], 2001, including his memories of growing up in Germany and escaping to the UK.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/1/43 and https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/2/1/43 Interview and transcript with Maggie Conu, 1999, whose parents were Jewish refugees from Nazi Germany.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/1/51 and https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/2/1/51 Interview and transcript with Jill Simmonds, 1999, including memories of German Jewish refugees on family farm.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/1/111 and https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/2/1/111 Interview and transcript with Nora Page-Wood, 1999, including taking in two German Jewish refugees during World War II.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/1/116 and https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D8497/2/1/116 Interview and transcript with an anonymous Jewish woman, 1999 (closed to the public until 2050) - no details available but may include relevant material.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/D4920/2/4/3/7 Biographical papers concerning the life and military career of Alfred 'Mac' McKenna who was in the Royal Gloucestershire Hussars and was involved in the liberation of Belsen concentration camp, including account of the war years 1939-1945.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/1/1/27, https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/2/1/1/34, https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/2/1/1/38, https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/2/1/2/21, https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/2/1/2/22 and https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/records/GCC/3/2/1/2/25 References in minutes of Gloucestershire County Council's Education Committee and its sub-committees to the provision of education for Jewish children and admission of refugees [presumably Jewish] to educational institutions in the county, 1939-1943.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/books/6032f48a-d989-4114-8482-10c5d73b429f Escaping Hitler: A Jewish boy's quest for freedom and his future by Phyllida Scrivens: biography of Gunter Stern, later Joe Stirling, a Jewish boy who arrived in the UK and was evacuated to Lydney in Gloucestershire between 1940 and 1943.
https://gloucestershire.epexio.com/books/d4549c1f-2900-4815-85fe-c5847cf2f592 Blood, Sweat and Tears: an oral history of the American Red Cross by Michele Turk, including a chapter on Warren [formerly Werner] Zorek (see above).

The National Collection of Aerial Photography includes photographs relating to the Second World War and its aftermath, including the Holocaust that can be searched at https://airphotofinder.ncap.org/map?c=0.00:0.00&z=4.00

Collections include:
MOL.2011.59 - Programme of Events, 'Holocaust Memorial Day 2008 Liverpool'
MOL.2012.17 - Holocaust Memorial Book, created by Association of Jewish Refugees, which tells the stories of many of the children who escaped Nazi Germany in the 1930s and settled in Liverpool.
MOL.2013.3.2 - Holocaust Memorial book, includes contributions from Merseyside based survivors, their partners and second-generation family members regarding their family members who died in the Holocaust. Includes DVD 'Never Forget' a film by Kim Ryan. Merseyside Holocaust Survivors - Their Memories. Commissioned by Liverpool City Council and FACT for Holocaust Memorial Day 2008.
MOL.2017.67.15 - Leaflet, 'Homotopia not Homophobia'. Homotopia and Merseyside Police present 'Project Triangle' a film by Tim Brunsden.  
MMM.2002.112.2 - Jewish order of service.  On the day of Fasting mourning and Prayer for the Victims of Mass Massacres of Jews in Nazi Lands.  Sunday 13th December 1942
MOL.2013.3.1 - Table cloth embroidered with the names (signatures) and home country of members of the Association of Jewish Refugees living in the Merseyside area over the last c. 10 years (2002 - 2012). First signature was Dr Gerald Jayson (Gert Jacobowski) in June 2002. The last signature 'Fay Healey, Danzig' in December 2012. All names embroidered by Dr Sylvia Jayson (wife of Gerald Jayson). Central embroidered Star of David with inscription 'Liverpool Jewish Refugees from Nazi Europe’.
Project Triangle involved 12 young lesbian, gay, bisexual & transgender people from Merseyside who took part in a five-day cultural exchange trip to Auschwitz and Warsaw and worked with a group of young Polish LGBT people from the Campaign Against Homophobia (KPH). The exchange provided the group with an appreciation of the Holocaust and fate of many LGBT people and the impact on European and LGBT social history as well as challenging past and present issues around hate crime. The film has since been developed into an educational resource pack for schools and colleges, enabling teachers to tackle homophobia and all forms of hate crime in schools.
